title: Boss: the codebreaker's bench
summary: Inspect bytes, build a one-time pad correctly, break one used twice, and replace weak randomness.

steps.title: Your bench
steps.body: Four jobs on a codebreaker's bench, each using what this module built: bytes and encodings, XOR, the one-time pad and its fatal reuse, and real randomness. Every program is deterministic, so where randomness is involved the tests check properties, never values.

steps.title: Byte inspector
prompt: Write a program that reads lines from standard input until the end, and for each line prints:
Example: the input line `Hi` prints `2 4869 SGk=`. An empty line prints `0  ` (count, then empty hex and empty Base64; trailing spaces are ignored).
steps.starter: // Read with Console.ReadLine() until it returns null.
hints: `while ((line = Console.ReadLine()) != null)` reads to the end.

steps.title: A correct one-time pad
prompt: - `(byte[] Cipher, byte[] Pad) Encrypt(string message)`: a **fresh** random pad from `RandomNumberGenerator`, exactly as long as the message's UTF-8 bytes, and the XOR of the two.
- `string Decrypt(byte[] cipher, byte[] pad)`: XOR back and decode as UTF-8. Throw `ArgumentException` if the lengths differ.
The tests check round trips (including non-ASCII text), lengths, and that encrypting the same message twice gives two different ciphertexts, because the pads differ.
solution: if (cipher.Length != pad.Length) throw new ArgumentException("The pad must be exactly as long as the ciphertext.");
template: {{CODE}}
var (dojoC, dojoPad) = Encrypt("attack at dawn");
Dojo.Eq("decrypting gives the message back", "attack at dawn", Decrypt(dojoC, dojoPad));
Dojo.Eq("the pad is as long as the message", 14, dojoPad.Length);
Dojo.Eq("the ciphertext is as long as the message", 14, dojoC.Length);
var (dojoC2, dojoPad2) = Encrypt("naïve café ☕");
Dojo.Eq("non-ASCII text survives", "naïve café ☕", Decrypt(dojoC2, dojoPad2));
var (dojoA, _) = Encrypt("same message");
var (dojoB, _) = Encrypt("same message");
Dojo.Check("two encryptions of one message differ", !dojoA.SequenceEqual(dojoB), "the same pad was used twice");
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("a short pad is rejected", () => Decrypt(dojoC, dojoPad[..5]));
hints: Use the UTF-8 byte count, not `message.Length`, for the pad size.

steps.title: Crib-drag a reused pad
prompt: Two equal-length orders were encrypted with the **same** pad. You know the first one starts with `"Transfer "`, but not the rest of it.

Print the part of the **second** message that this known prefix reveals (as many characters as the prefix is long), then on a second line print how many positions of the two messages hold the **same** character (where `c1[i] == c2[i]`; reuse leaks even that).
hints: `c1[i] ^ c2[i]` is `p1[i] ^ p2[i]`; XOR the crib in to leave `p2[i]`.
Equal ciphertext bytes under the same pad mean equal plaintext bytes.

steps.title: Session ids that cannot be guessed
prompt: Write `string NewSessionId()` (32 random bytes, lowercase hex, so 64 characters) and `string NewPin()` (6 digits, every digit equally likely, so `GetString` or `GetInt32`, never `%` on a byte).
Then write `bool LooksLikeSessionId(string s)` that accepts exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, so a server can reject malformed ids before looking them up.
solution: bool LooksLikeSessionId(string s) => s.Length == 64 && s.All(c => c is >= '0' and <= '9' or >= 'a' and <= 'f');
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoIds = Enumerable.Range(0, 50).Select(_ => NewSessionId()).ToList();
Dojo.Check("session ids look valid", dojoIds.All(LooksLikeSessionId), "a generated id failed LooksLikeSessionId");
Dojo.Eq("50 session ids are all different", 50, dojoIds.Distinct().Count());
Dojo.Check("uppercase hex is rejected", !LooksLikeSessionId(new string('A', 64)), "accepted uppercase");
Dojo.Check("63 characters are rejected", !LooksLikeSessionId(new string('a', 63)), "accepted a short id");
Dojo.Check("non-hex is rejected", !LooksLikeSessionId(new string('g', 64)), "accepted 'g'");
var dojoPins = Enumerable.Range(0, 2000).Select(_ => NewPin()).ToList();
Dojo.Check("PINs are 6 digits", dojoPins.All(p => p.Length == 6 && p.All(char.IsAsciiDigit)), "a PIN was not 6 digits");
var dojoCounts = dojoPins.SelectMany(p => p).GroupBy(c => c).ToDictionary(g => g.Key, g => g.Count());
Dojo.Check("all ten digits appear", dojoCounts.Count == 10, "some digit never appeared in 12,000 draws");
